title: Weight-space programming: models that read and write weights, audited
summary: The Sparks of Weight-Space Programming experiments, story by story: models reading small networks' weights, writing game players from zero, and the two-layer edit that unstuck Qwen's reasoning loops. Plus the laptop reproduction, a look inside the loop, the lineage from hypernetworks to refusal directions, and the critique that bundling the results overstates them.

topics: deep dive: weight-space programming: models that read and write weights
concepts_taught: weight-space programming: a general-purpose model reading and writing a network's weights directly from a plain-language goal, without gradient descent — and why its experiments split into tool-free raw-weight reading on tiny networks (17K-172K weights) versus Python-assisted interpretability and editing on real language models

reading a network's purpose from its weights by structure rather than simulation: input-channel concentration and output-action separation in tiny game policies, copying heads as a fingerprint of code, and the sycophancy case that failed from weights alone but succeeded with attention-pattern access
writing networks from zero as programming in matrix entries (Breakout 517 vs PPO's 25, losses on Seaquest and Asterix), and one-shot patches to a failing policy

removing an obstacle versus adding an ability: the Qwen3.5-0.8B reasoning-loop edit (one direction in two MLP layers, 0.016% of weights, MATH-500 7.9 to 48.1) against the Gemma 3 270M null result, and why reversing a direction beat plain ablation
the lineage of weight-space methods: hypernetworks, predicting accuracy from weights, rank-one model editing, task arithmetic, and single-direction refusal ablation
listener_note: spend only 3-4 minutes on each of the mini-dives. Give space for multiple stories instead
